title.en: Practical 2: Focal length of a convex lens

text.en: A lens can focus a distant tree on a screen on your desk.

The aim is to find the focal length of a convex lens by the distant object method and by the uv method. The apparatus is a convex lens, a stand, a wire gauze object, a screen and a measuring scale.
In the distant object method, fix the lens near a window, get a sharp inverted diminished image of a distant tree or building on the screen and measure the lens-to-screen distance, which is about f. In the uv method, place the wire gauze object beyond 2f, adjust the screen for a sharp image and measure u and v.
The focal length is f = uv / (u + v). Repeat for different positions: u greater than 2f gives a diminished image, u = 2f gives a same-size image and u less than 2f gives a magnified image.
